title: Assembly Language
description: Write x86-64 assembly by hand and see what your C compiler really produces. Start with a function that returns a value, then learn the registers and calling convention, compare and branch to build loops over memory, and use the stack to save registers and call your own functions. Every exercise is graded by C tests that call your code. Uses GNU assembler Intel syntax and needs gcc or clang; Apple Silicon Macs run the code under Rosetta.
author: FreeKnowledge contributors
